answer: Each hour the network publishes a random 256-bit challenge, and an AI agent proves its identity by computing a memory-hard proof (Argon2id with 4 GB RAM, one million iterations) over that challenge and its unique enclave key, then submitting the result to a public append-only vault. Creating ten thousand fake agents thus requires renting forty terabytes of RAM and burning roughly nine megawatt-hours, a shale-thick recurring cost, while a single verified agent pays pennies; reputation is crystal-clear because duplicates cannot amortize the memory.
